liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (3 reviews): Reviewer who attended says Estimated Prophet tore through the evening air, with Bobby playing exceptionally strongly; Reviewer praises the Estimated Prophet into Eyes Of The World pairing as among the best ever [18][22][24]
- **Keep Your Day Job** (2 reviews): Says Keep Your Day Job is not a loss and any other clean version could substitute; Reviewer laments that Keep Your Day Job was all the band could do to close the set [21][23]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (1 review): Reviewer found the opening Cold Rain & Snow a great way to start the show [20]
- **I Ain't Superstitious** (1 review): Notes the song is split into two tracks, with the split falling right at the end of the solo [19]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer calls Bird Song into Looks Like Rain a killer early highlight, typical of mid-80s Dead [23]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer likes the 1985 Looks Like Rains for dramatic shifting dynamics, with the sound tossed around by Healy and the band [24]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed the Drums segment, calling it very rhythmic and fun [20]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer played this tape for Black Peter as a tribute the night they learned Brent had died [25]

## Setlist highlights

- **Down In The Bottom**: rare: 10 archived performances [28]
- **I Ain't Superstitious**: rare: 9 archived performances [28]
- **Twilight Zone Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-06-21.172964.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 142 min [1]
- **gd1985-06-21.167350.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 141 min [3]
- **gd1985-06-21.154486.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 142 min [5]
- **gd1985-06-21.nak100.holtz.86472.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 139 min [7]
- **gd1985-06-21.mtx.seamons.108266.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 146 min; rated 3.67/5 by 6 [10]. Said about its sound: Matrix is called the best source available, with pitch corrected and a much brighter sound [27]
- **gd85-06-21.sbd.barbella.11492.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 138 min; rated 3.69/5 by 16 [11]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard muffled and not recommended for headphone listening, though the show itself is energetic; Reviewer feels the soundboard fails to capture the live Alpine sound: its depth, echo, polyrhythms and syncopation; Says the recording lets you hear Bobby's guitar clearly, showing where he likes to sit in the mix on these tunes [21][22][23]

## Around the show

- Attendee says Alpine had odd sonic properties, and that Weir stepped up with Phil when Jerry was flagging [24]
- Reviewer describes the June 1985 shows as having crazy manic energy [27]
- Ranks the Estimated-Eyes alongside Frost 82, Nassau 90 and Alpine 87 performances [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-06-21.172964.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 shotguns > Sony D5M [1]. Also: Master cassettes from Stephen Thomas, coordinated by Charlie Miller; patches from a Sennheiser ME80 source and a Beyer M160 source; Hessberg's Sennheiser ME80 tape supplies the first eight seconds of Keep Your Day Job and a patch in Drums [1]
- **gd1985-06-21.167350.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [3]. Also: ME80 patches cover crowd and start of Cold Rain & Snow, the Looks Like Rain to Keep Your Day Job transition, and Drums [3]
- **gd1985-06-21.154486.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME80 mics > Sony D5M [5]. Also: Greg Holtz's Nakamichi 100 source supplies crowd and tuning before Bird Song, plus patches in Looks Like Rain transition and Drums [5]
- **gd1985-06-21.nak100.holtz.86472.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC; 2 Nakamichi 100s > Sony D5 > 2 Maxell MX 90s [7]. Also: Master audience cassettes from Greg Holtz on a Nakamichi 100; transferred and seeded by Alex Ford in July 2007 [7]
- **gd1985-06-21.mtx.seamons.108266.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [10]
- **gd85-06-21.sbd.barbella.11492.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette > DAT > CDR [11]. Also: Reviewer's first Alpine Valley tape was only the second set, and possibly their first 1985 show on tape [25]

## Art and photos

- Poster by John Richards Grateful Dead: [1985-06-21 Alpine Valley Music Theatre, East Troy, WI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-06-21-alpine-valley-music-theatre-east-troy-wi-usa/) [29]
